app.version: 0.2.47 with the team; going to Apple for outside testers
app.summary:
Smidgeon Scholars, 12 November 2026. Test build 0.2.26 is with testers. This replaces the older "Where the app is now" (0.1.21). Jennie decides what children learn and every word they and their grown-ups hear; Seth's side builds it. Anything marked a draft is Seth's placeholder wording waiting for Jennie.

Five tabs: Today, Journal, Flock, Help me (call Jennie), Settings.

TODAY: one feeling a day, the same for every family (e.g. "The Nervous Feeling"). A journey map of about ten stops in a fixed order: mailbox (the feeling arrives as a group chat with Smidgeon and Jennie), pinwheel (breathing), drum (move your body), Feeling Mirror (make the face, then "What does nervous look like to you? Practice with your grown-up."), Feeling Pairs, a call with Jennie (the child says how they feel; kept on the phone only), the nest, Sun/Cloud/Rainbow, and a present. Each stop ends with a celebration line. The day ends at home: Smidgeon on the windowsill at lunch, dinner, tidy-up or bedtime, with a question and a helper job. The path is once a day.

JOURNAL: a calendar of days, each a postcard: Smidgeon acting out the feeling, the date as a stamp, coins for what we did, and what we said as chat bubbles. How I felt (pick a face) and What we did (coins in Me, Nest, The Flock). A deed done 1/3/5/10 times becomes copper/bronze/silver/gold. Filling in the day is a Stories-style sequence. "Days together" never resets: no broken streaks.

FLOCK (anonymous): a feed of families' postcards with each family's emoji and a made-up kind name, never real names, and hearts. Example families fill it until real ones join. Sharing is off until a grown-up turns it on. Nothing is sent anywhere yet: the real feed (Apple's CloudKit) waits for a children's-privacy (COPPA) review and Jennie's approval of the copy.

HELP ME: call Jennie any time about one feeling.

SETTINGS: tips and printouts, emoji and skin tone, save what we tell Jennie, read everything aloud, flock sharing, narrator voice.

PRINCIPLES: tandem (child and grown-up together); Smidgeon shows, Jennie coaches; steam shows how big a feeling is, never good or bad; never marked wrong; built for pre-readers; resolve and pause before moving on; no red except hang-up and hearts.

HOW TO HELP: suggest wording, order and what children learn in these terms, so Seth's side can drop it straight in. Most words and stories change without a new app version.

tasks.title: Smidgeon's Sun, Cloud and Rainbow lines: 12 of each
tasks.detail:
Smidgeon used to say the same three lines every day, which felt stale. Now he picks one of these each time, never one of the last few he said. They're drafts in his voice, already recorded for testing: tell us which to keep, change or drop, or send your own.

SUN (something that brought joy):
1. I loved building my tower with Pip.
2. I found a shiny feather on the path!
3. Wren and I splashed in a puddle. Splash!
4. I ate my very favourite seeds at lunch.
5. Pip shared her blanket with me. So cosy!
6. I saw a butterfly with orange wings!
7. I flew all the way to the big tree by myself.
8. Robin told me a funny joke, and I giggled and giggled.
9. I helped my grown-up water the flowers.
10. I sang my coo-coo song, and everyone clapped!
11. The sun was warm on my feathers. Ahh.
12. I made a new friend at the pond.

CLOUD (something hard):
1. My tower fell down. That was hard.
2. I wanted the red swing, but someone else was on it.
3. I dropped my snack in the mud. Oh no.
4. Pip didn't want to play with me today. That felt sad.
5. The thunder was loud, and I felt scared.
6. I tried to fly over the fence, and I bumped my wing.
7. I had to stop playing when it was time to go home.
8. My feathers got all tangled in the wind.
9. I lost my favourite feather. I looked everywhere.
10. I couldn't find the right words, and I got frustrated.
11. It rained, so we couldn't play outside.
12. I said something unkind, and then I felt sorry.

RAINBOW (looking forward to):
1. Tomorrow is picnic day!
2. We are going to visit family!
3. I can't wait to splash in the pond again.
4. Pip and I are going to build the tallest tower ever.
5. I'm going to try flying to the top of the bell tower.
6. Tomorrow we'll look for shiny feathers together.
7. I can't wait to see the stars tonight.
8. Wren is coming over to play!
9. I'm going to learn a brand-new song.
10. Tomorrow I'll give Robin the drawing I made.
11. I'm looking forward to a big, cosy sleep.
12. We're going to plant seeds in the garden!

tasks.title: Your three learning games: the choices we made
tasks.detail: Built from your docs and in the new test build; the pictures are temporary while we test how they play. Tell us what to change. REMEMBER THREE: same order; Smidgeon asks the child to say them to their grown-up, then they tap them in order from five pictures (three plus two extras: too many?); grows to four after three easy rounds in a row, back to three after a hard one; it lives inside What Did Smidgeon Carry? as see it / hear it. SMIDGEON COUNTS: counts to 10 for now (a 20 setting for four-year-olds, with 12 to 15 in focus, can come next); skills open in your order, each after three first-try successes; both your versions are built (a mix, or one skill a day): which one? Rooftop Hop: child and grown-up take turns rolling for one Smidgeon, dots 1 to 3 at first, bench rest stops are breathing breaks, star roofs bring a skill; Message Route ends with a mailbox or house-number moment. Your try-later lines are used as written; the house-number and adding ones are drafts. Printables later. SMIDGEON'S LETTERS: one of Smidgeon's days a week, up to two new letters a play, then one word; capitals beside lowercase when meeting a letter, lowercase for reading; tracing comes later. The meet lines ("Look! The sun is up.") are drafts: do any scenes or words not fit Smidgeon's world? Digraphs and long vowels later.

tasks.title: Letter sounds
tasks.detail: Smidgeon's Letters is built from your phonics plan and plays placeholder sounds until yours arrive; each recording replaces its placeholder on its own. (24 Nov: the computer-made stand-ins are now much closer to your rule, with short vowels, quick clipped stops, hard c and g, and no "uh" after the letters, so the blending words sound better too. A few still need your real voice: see "Letter sounds to record for real".) Pure sounds only (/s/, not "suh"); hold the stretchy ones, keep the bouncy ones crisp; c as /k/, g as /g/, qu as /kw/, x as /ks/. The 26 sounds, by Smidgeon's day: Morning at home: s /sss/ (sun), a /a/ (apple), t /t/ (toast), p /p/ (pan); The mail route: i /i/ (inchworm), n /nnn/ (nest), m /mmm/ (mailbox), d /d/ (door); The garden and pond: g /g/ (gate), o /o/ (otter), c /k/ (cat), k /k/ (kite); A rainy day: r /rrr/ (rain), e /e/ (envelope), u /u/ (umbrella), h /h/ (hat); The park: b /b/ (bus), f /fff/ (feather), l /lll/ (leaf); Lunch and deliveries: j /j/ (jam), w /w/ (worm), v /vvv/ (van), x /ks/ (box); Bedtime: y /y/ (yawn), z /zzz/ (zip), qu /kw/ (quilt). Then each blending word, slowly then quickly ("/s/ /a/ /t/... sat!"): Morning at home: sat, pat, tap, at; The mail route: pin, tin, sit, nap, man, mad, dip, mat; The garden and pond: dog, cat, cap, cot, kid, kit, pot, top, mop; A rainy day: red, hen, ten, net, sun, mud, rug, cup, hug, hot; The park: bed, bus, bug, fan, fig, fun, leg, lip, log; Lunch and deliveries: jam, jog, van, vet, wet, web, wig, box, fox, six; Bedtime: yes, yum, zip, zap, quiz, quit. File names (letter_s, blend_sat…) are in docs/LETTER-SOUNDS.md. Same session as the voice sample is fine.

tasks.title: Letter sounds to record for real
tasks.detail: The computer voice can't make a clean, pure letter sound, so these still need a human recording (the rule for all of them: a pure sound, short vowels, hard c and g, and nothing after the sound, so /b/ and never "buh"). First, the quick stop sounds, which are now only a tiny click from the computer voice and need a real short, clipped sound: b, c, d, g, j, k, p, t, w, y, and qu (/kw/). Second, the short vowels a (apple) and o (otter), which come from the computer saying "at" and "ox" and cutting out the middle; please say them on their own. Third, x as /ks/ and h as a soft breath, which are stitched together by the computer. Fourth, e, i and u, which are fine for now but have never been checked by ear against a short vowel. The long hummy sounds (s, f, m, n, l, r, v, z) are close to right already and can be done last. Every blending word is built from the letter sounds, so once yours are in, the blends rebuild from them. Also, Jennie: the key word for e is still envelope; should it be egg? That is your call, so nothing was changed.

tasks.title: New draft words since 0.2.26
tasks.detail: Drafts added in 0.2.27 and 0.2.28: the welcome's emoji page now says "Pick your emoji. It shows who's talking in your journal, and it's your name in the flock."; the emoji choosers have sections (Kids, Pets, Farm, Wild, Birds, Sea, Bugs, Dinos & dragons, Make-believe) and say "Your name in the flock" / "Tap to choose"; grown-ups have friendly names (Teacher, Grandma, Builder); coins earned that day appear on the journal page as "Earned the Silver Book!" with the deed underneath; a day with nothing written says "Nothing written down this day."

tasks.title: 18 new Story Path stories (two for every feeling)
tasks.detail: Families who play every day kept meeting the same story: each feeling had one, and a feeling comes round every 9 days. These are 18 drafts, two per feeling, each with a different friend, place and way through. They're already in the app as drafts so Seth can try them. Read each one and reply on it: approve, or say what to change. Approved so far: 11 of 18; 7 still to read.
tasks.answer: Not related but a thought for the welcome message in the app. Who he is. Smidgeon is a carrier pigeon. He carries messages between a child's inner emotional world and the adults who love them. He is "a journal for children who can't write yet."

tasks.title: New draft words from 13 November
tasks.detail: Sun, Cloud and Rainbow now opens with you saying: "Now let's share our sun, our cloud and our rainbow. Your sun is something that brought you joy today. Your cloud is something that was hard. Your rainbow is something you're looking forward to." (Seth wonders if it's too long for 3–5s.) Today's journal page title is "A … day" until a feeling is picked, then "A sad day"; its prompts are "I told Jennie…", "My sun today was…", "My cloud today was…", "My rainbow is…", "What I did today…"; a past day with nothing written says "Nothing written down this day."; the feeling picker asks "How are you feeling today?". The finished day's button: "Fill in today's journal" / "See today's journal".

tasks.title: Pick Smidgeon's new voice
tasks.detail: Listen to today's voice and eight candidates (A to H), each saying the same calm, sad and bright lines. Reply here with the letter you like, or two letters to mix, and all of Smidgeon's lines will be re-recorded in that voice.

tasks.title: "Goodbye, Robin": Robin now moves away
tasks.detail:
Robin used to go to visit his grandma "for a long time", which could sound like something sadder. Now Robin's family moves to a new home, and the story ends on remembering a friend by honouring the memories: looking at pictures, talking about them, feeling grateful, and knowing the friendship lives on in your heart. New ending below, drafts for you to approve, already recorded for testing: tell us what to keep or change.

Story:
• "My family is moving to a new home, far away," said Robin. Smidgeon's wings drooped.
• (unchanged) Pretend he doesn't care / Say "I'll miss you", and the hug.
• NEW: Robin waved goodbye. "I'll always remember you!"
• NEW: They looked at pictures of Robin and felt thankful. A friend lives in your heart (the talking about the fun is in the grown-up's "Then you can say" line).

Talk about it together:
• For the child: Robin's family moved to a new home, far away.
• Then you can say: "You're sad Robin moved away." / "What will you remember most about Robin?" / NEW: "Let's look at pictures of Robin and talk about the fun."

tasks.title: The welcome now introduces Smidgeon as a carrier pigeon
tasks.detail:
Your idea is on the second welcome page, read aloud, with Smidgeon holding an envelope. We changed your words a little to fit the page; tell us if you'd like them back as you wrote them, or changed:

"This is Smidgeon, a small carrier pigeon with big feelings. He carries messages between your child's inside world and the grown-ups who love them. He's a journal for children who can't write yet."

tasks.title: Smidgeon's feelings inside the games
tasks.detail:
Your idea is in Rooftop Hop, Remember Three, Letters and the counting moments. Nothing is marked wrong any more: a wrong tap just dips softly. Smidgeon says these, in his own voice (drafts, already recorded):

• After a second miss (he looks frustrated): "Grr, two tries and not yet! That's frustrating. Let's take a big breath, and look again."
• When they get it after that: "We kept trying, and we got it! That makes me happy."
• At the end of the game, one of two: "We did the whole thing. I feel proud!" or "You stuck with it and didn't give up!" (new, never the same one twice in a row)

A right answer on the first try gets no extra words, so the happy line stays special. Tell us what to change.

tasks.title: Families now pick their flock name's kind word
tasks.detail:
Your idea: in the welcome and in Settings, families tap a kind word for their pretend flock name ("Brave Bunny", "Dreamy Dino"). Words that start with the same letter as their emoji come first, then: Little, Brave, Gentle, Busy, Sunny, Sleepy, Hopping, Cosy, Curious, Merry, Quiet, Bouncy. Only the pretend name is ever shown to other families.

The letter words (drafts): Artsy, Awesome · Brave, Bouncy, Busy · Curious, Cosy, Cheery · Daring, Dreamy, Dancing · Eager, Easygoing · Friendly, Fuzzy, Funny · Gentle, Giggly, Glad · Happy, Hopping, Helpful · Jolly, Jumpy · Kind · Lucky, Little, Lovely · Merry, Mighty, Mellow · Nifty, Nice · Outgoing, Outdoorsy · Peppy, Playful, Proud · Quiet, Quick · Rosy, Rolling · Sunny, Silly, Sleepy · Tiny, Twinkly, Thoughtful · Upbeat · Wiggly, Wise, Wonderful · Zippy.

We took out "Kooky" and "Zany" in case they read as teasing. Tell us any to add, drop or change.

tasks.title: A celebration every 7 days together
tasks.detail:
Your idea: every 7 days together (not in a row: 7, 14, 21…) the family's own celebration card appears in the flock, and a little gold coin marks that day on the journal calendar. 30, 50 and 100 days stay extra special.

The weekly card's words (draft): "14 days together!" / "Seven more days of growing together."
The 30, 50 and 100 card: "30 days together!" / "A day together, again and again."

tasks.title: Rooftop Hop: a counting-on level
tasks.detail:
Your idea: once a child reads the 5-dot die at a glance, Rooftop Hop moves up a level. The roofs show numbers, and Smidgeon counts on from where he is: on roof 4, rolling 3, they count "5, 6, 7". Near the end the die can roll more than the roofs left, and they count on all the way home.

New lines (drafts, recorded):
• Smidgeon, before each roll's hops: "<his roof number>. Let's count on!"
• When the roll was bigger than the roofs left: "We only needed some of the dots. We counted on all the way home!"

tasks.title: "What we did": a row for your own
tasks.detail:
Your idea: the 18 coins stay, and there's a fourth group, "Ours", where a grown-up adds their own (up to six), like "Fed the cat". It shows as a fourth row on "What we did" and a tab in the journal.

Words (drafts): "Ours" · "Add your own" · "Something we did" · "e.g. Fed the cat" · "Add" · "Cancel" · "Remove".

tasks.title: Smidgeon's Letters: a sound-matching step
tasks.detail:
From your Phonics Plan v2: after Smidgeon meets the day's letters, three quick questions using only letters met so far, before the blending word. They take turns: hear a pure sound and tap the capital letter that makes it, or see a capital and tap the picture that starts with its sound (sun, apple…). C and K never appear together as choices. Two misses: Smidgeon is frustrated, then happy when they get it; nothing is marked wrong.

Words (drafts, recorded): "Which letter makes this sound?" · "Which one starts with this sound?" · "Listen again."

tasks.title: Age and birthday, and a birthday hello
tasks.detail:
Seth's idea: the welcome now asks the child's age and birthday (month and day), kept only on the phone. On their birthday Smidgeon celebrates once, and a little cake marks the day in the journal. Solo mode and make-your-own-bird open at 5 and up.

Words (drafts): "How old is your little one?" · "When's their birthday?" · "Just for birthday hellos. It stays on this phone." · "Happy birthday!" · "You're 5 today!"

tasks.title: Make your own bird (first version, 5 and up)
tasks.detail:
Your idea, small first version: a child picks a colour (Berry, Sunset, Acorn, Meadow, Forest, Lagoon) and a name, then fills in their bird's story one blank at a time with picture choices or their own words. Their bird then appears beside Smidgeon in the day's story.

Words (drafts): "Make your own bird!" · "What's your bird called?" (Pip-squeak, Feathers, Sunny, Bean, Puff, Ziggy) · "<Name> loves ____" (berries, kites, splashing, singing) · "<Name>'s favourite place is ____" (the big tree, the pond, the nest, the garden) · "When <Name> feels frustrated, it ____" (takes a big breath, asks for a hug, goes for a walk, says how it feels) · "Meet <Name>!"

tasks.title: "What's new" for families who started earlier
tasks.detail:
Seth's idea: families who did the welcome before something new was added see one small "New" note above the day's button (at most one a day; Later, or No thanks), and all of them are listed in Settings.

Words (drafts): "New: add their birthday" / "We'll celebrate with Smidgeon on the day. It stays on this phone." · "New: pick your flock name" / "Choose the kind word in your pretend flock name, like Dreamy Dino." · "New: add your own coins" / "In \"What we did\", grown-ups can now add their own things, like \"Fed the cat\"."

tasks.title: Play on my own (5 and up)
tasks.detail:
Seth's call: once a child is 5 or older (from the age in the welcome), Home shows an "On my own" button. It opens a corner with Rooftop Hop, Smidgeon's Letters, Remember Three and their own bird, to play without a grown-up (in Rooftop Hop the child takes every turn). The feelings journey stays something you do together.

Words (drafts): "Play on my own" · "On my own" · "Make your own bird" / "My bird: Sunny" · What's new: "New: play on my own" / "For 5 and up: the learning games to play on their own, and make their own bird."

tasks.title: Pick the app icon: A to F
tasks.detail: The six options from 16 November, each shown next to today's icon at real home-screen size on a light and a dark wallpaper. A (cheering, starburst) and C (flying with a letter) were the favourites. Reply with your letter (or "keep today's"). The app keeps today's icon until one is picked.

tasks.title: End-of-day reading: new lines so nothing is missed
tasks.detail:
Sandie noticed the end-of-day reading missed one or two of the things we did. It now reads everything the family did that day, in the day's order, one bubble each, repeats included. The ones that already had a line (path, breathing, mirror, matching, nest, how big) keep their feeling-named lines. These are new short drafts in the narrator's voice, already recorded for testing: tell us which to keep, change or drop, or send your own.

1. Energy burst: We did an energy burst and breathed back to still.
2. Your call (read only if you did the call, not if you chose later): We talked with Jennie on the phone.
3. Message route: We walked a kind note across the park.
4. Remember three: We remembered three things, in order.
5. Rooftop hop: We counted the hops up the rooftops.
6. Letters: We met new letters and read a word.
7. Any other game we haven't written for: We played a game together.

Should lines 1 to 3 name the feeling like the others do ("You breathed with Smidgeon when he felt happy")? Say so and we will write nine each.

Your three Academic Skills plans are built in the test app, following your answers: Remember Three (see it / hear it, same order, say it to your grown-up then tap, grows to four after three easy rounds) inside What Did Smidgeon Carry?; Smidgeon Counts' seven skills in Rooftop Hop and Message Route (count to 10 for now, unlocking in your order); Smidgeon's Letters with all 26 letters over your seven days, capitals beside lowercase, one of Smidgeon's days a week, placeholder sounds until you record. The words are drafts for you; tracing comes later. The letter-sounds task now lists every recording.
